note: The lexer's MSSTRING rule returns an MS_STRING token for every quoted string inside the PROJECTION block, copying the attacker-controlled text into msyystring_buffer. The number of such tokens is entirely controlled by the input map file.
loadProjection() runs an unbounded token loop that consumes MS_STRING/MS_AUTO tokens until END; no limit is imposed on how many projection argument tokens are accepted.

Root cause: i is incremented for every MS_STRING/MS_AUTO token without being checked against MS_MAXPROJARGS (20). p->args was allocated with only MS_MAXPROJARGS entries in msInitProjection(), so once more than 20 tokens are read, the index used by the next write is out of range.
Sink: the 21st token (i==20) writes a char* pointer past the end of the 20-entry p->args heap allocation, i.e. a WRITE heap-buffer-overflow detected by ASan inside loadProjection().
